correctness.rationale: Sobolewski Theorem 1.4 guarantees first-change finiteness for d>=3, and r(3)=r(6)=1 handles d=1,2; direct bit-pair counting shows r(2n)=r(n), excluding even first-change indices. The duplicated-L-bit identity is an exact parity identity. For each odd k>=3 the maximal odd a<=Q/(k-1) satisfies (k-2)a<Q<=ka<2Q, forcing r(jd)=0 for j<k and r(kd)=1. All quantifiers are explicit; k=1 and infinite witnesses covered. The smallest Q gives d<32k^3. The supplied standalone Python checker independently recomputes finite consequences.

value.rationale: This settles the explicitly conjectured Rudin–Shapiro v=11 origin-spectrum in Problem 8 of Sobolewski (arXiv:2204.05287, Section 6): every positive odd length occurs and no even length does. It is a natural complete invariant classification, and the polynomial witness bound adds effective constructive content. This is not a known-table transcription nor an arbitrary special case.
